1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, Government intended to acquire about 2636 Bigha 18 Biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme'
under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
LAC no. 227/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Mahavir Singh & Ors. Vs.
Union of India
Page no. 2 of 11 3.

The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2001/L&B/LA/28199 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2636 Bigha 18 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari), Delhi.

The LAC (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2636 Bighas 18 Biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/
per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are the recorded owner/bhumidhar of the land comprised in Khasra no. 8//4 (416) i.e. total area measuring 04 Bighas and 16 Biswas, having share as per the revenue record, situated in the revenue estate of Village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari), Delhi (in short, the said land).
5.

It is stated that the Award passed by the ld. LAC is not acceptable to the petitioners and,
therefore, this reference has been filed with a view to reassess the market value of the land which has been wrongly assessed by the LAC.
LAC no. 227/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Mahavir Singh & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 3 of 11 6.

i) The land of the petitioner is situated in Village K. S. Nagar (Patti Nithari), Delhi and is well connected with metaled roads from all sides and at the time of acquisition Mahavir Singh Ors. sentences.text:
The land of petitioner is levelled and as such gives handsome crops income 2-3 times in a year to the petitioner and some part of the land is developed as colony and the petitioners also claims for loss of livelihood and also loss of income interalia on the following amongst other grounds.
ii) The land of the petitioner is situated near the National Highway No. 10, Rohtak Road, Delhi and has great potential value as a perfect Building/ Commercial site.
Commercial and Residential activities have commenced all around the land of the petitioner and are going on since more than 12 years.
All kinds of civic amenities like electricity, water, road, bus service, telephone, school, college, etc are easily available to the land of the petitioners,
Thus, the land of petitioners has great value being developed and a perfect residential and commercial site.
iii) The Land of the petitioners is approachable by metaled road and is very close to Nangloi township and Mundka Industrial Area and the same were fully developed at the time of notification.

There are many residential colonies such as Pratap Vihar, Aman Vihar, Sultanpuri, Prem Nagar,
Karan Vihar and Nangloi Township, etc which are existing since 1993 near the land of the petitioner and LAC no. 227/ 2016 (Award No. 25/200506/DC(NW)) Mahavir Singh & Ors. Vs. Union of India Page no. 4 of 11 Govt. is also going to regularise the said buildings and provide all the civic amenities thereafter.

sentences.text: Therefore, the price of the acquired land should have been assessed minimum @ Rs 10,000/- per sq. yards.

iv) The land of the petitioners have been covered by the other revenue estate such as Sultanpuri,
Nithari, Pooth Kalan, Nangloi which are well developed by way of construction of colonies and have great potential value.
Moreover, the petitioners have solid proof regarding the higher market value of land which is not less than Rs. 10,000/- and the same may be produced at the time of evidence before the Court.

It is also alleged that the Government police has not been properly implemented because the indicative price fixed by the Government is totally wrong and illegal and the same should be ratify and compensation be paid to the petitioners.
v) The Government Policy has not been properly implemented because the indicative price fixed by the Government is totally wrong and illegal.
Further, the LAC has failed to consider to assessing the value of standing trees, tubewell and structures.

7. It is stated that in view of these facts and circumstances and keeping in view the consideration of the petitioners, petitioners are claiming compensation for their acquired land at Rs. 10,000/- per sq.
yards and Rs. 5 lakhs for damages as sustained by compulsory acquisition and cost of boaring and structure be awarded alongwith statutory benefits and interest under LA Act and enhanced compensation be released to the petitioners and the category of land be rectified.

sentences.text: The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioners.
It is settled preposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the acquired land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioner.
The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP v. Ram Kumari Devi (1996) 8 SCC 577 as well as in State of UP and Anr.

17.

During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 18.10.2023 and Ld.

18.

19. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Kirari Suleman Nagar (Patti Nithari) is covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.

20. In the case of Ajit Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Mubarkpur Dabas acquired through Award No. 25 of 200506 dated 06.02.2006 as Rs.
19,45,800/ per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs. 3,75,800/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Ajit Singh (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Ajit Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,45,800/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/ per acre.
21. The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
ISSUE NO. 2/ RELIEF 22.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs: (1) Fair Market value of land of petitioner @ Rs.19,45,800/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.

(2) Additional amount @ 12% (
in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act).
